newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico minister aims for 6 pct growth in long term.
newsitem.headline: Mexico minister aims for 6 pct growth in long term.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillero Ortiz said on Friday that Mexico needed to achieve economic growth rates of about six percent, acknowledging that next year's target of four percent was inadequate.

"We are convinced that the four percent growth that we are proposing for next year, though it is achievable, is insufficient," Ortiz told the Mexican Congress during an appearance to defend his 1997 budget proposal.
"We have to ... define what are the elements that all sectors of society should contribute in order to achieve growth of six percent and above," he said.
Ortiz said a strengthening economy already was being reflected in more jobs.
He said consumer demand would recover somewhat next year, though retail spending would not reach as high as it did two years ago, before the country suffered its peso crash.

Criticized by opposition lawmakers for a recovery that looks good on paper but has not filtered down to ordinary Mexicans, Ortiz said he believed the economic upturn would become more tangible next year.
He said wage contracts were already being negotiated above inflation rates, which would mean a reversal of the trend of falling real wages during the past two years.
His budget also includes a sharp increase in public investment, which he said would play a key role in stoking the recovery.
